 1               P R O C E E D I N G S

 2                ACTING PRESIDENT GRIFFO:   The 

 3   Senate will come to order.  

 4                I ask all present to please rise 

 5   and join with me as we recite the Pledge of 

 6   Allegiance to our Flag.

 7                (Whereupon, the assemblage recited 

 8   the Pledge of Allegiance to the Flag.)

 9                ACTING PRESIDENT GRIFFO:   Today's 

10   invocation will be offered by Pastor Duke 

11   Hergatt, from Temple Baptist Church in 

12   Waterford.  

13                Pastor?

14                PASTOR HERGATT:   It's a great 

15   honor for me to be here today.  

16                May we pray.  

17                Our Father Who art in heaven, 

18   hallowed be Thy name.  O Lord, You know I prayed 

19   to these words 10,000 times and was clueless to 

20   what they really meant.  Forgive us of any 

21   outward show and our inward ignorance.  

22                You became our Father when we by 

23   faith chose to believe in Your gospel and bowed 

24   our hearts to the Savior of the world You gave 

25   so graciously that first Christmas night.  


                                                                275

 1                Hallowed be Thy name, as John the 

 2   Baptist prayed.  O Lord, You must increase, we 

 3   must decrease.  Be glorified at our expense.  We 

 4   are here to serve You.  Let he that be great 

 5   among us be servants, You said.  And we ask not 

 6   that You would serve us.  

 7                Please forgive us our selfish 

 8   ambitions.  May we never forget Your kingdom is 

 9   coming and Your will will be done on that day 

10   when all wrongs will be righted and every knee 

11   will bow.  Injustice will be over, and the meek 

12   shall inherit the earth.  And the lion will lie 

13   down with the lamb.  Your will be done on earth 

14   today, right here, right now in this chamber of 

15   the New York State Senate.  May Your will, not 

16   public opinion or political correctness, 

17   prevail.  

18                We thank You today for our daily 

19   bread and the abundance that all we in this 

20   chamber so enjoy.  And we pray for those less 

21   fortunate than us.  And forgive us our 

22   trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass 

23   against us.  Forgive our unbelief which keeps us 

24   from Your blessings.  Forgive our pride and our 

25   self-centeredness.  Convict and cleanse our 


                                                                276

 1   representatives of all fraud, corruption and 

 2   self-will.  

 3                Help us to forgive the fallen and 

 4   those who have sinned against us.  And lead us 

 5   not into temptation, which is so especially 

 6   powerful here in this place.  May our 

 7   representatives say no to bribes and dishonest 

 8   and secret financial gain.  Please, Father, 

 9   deliver them from this evil.  

10                We pray for those who have fallen 

11   to be exposed, to confess, to repent.  We pray 

12   for them to be restored to Your grace and their 

13   family's love.  

14                May we be reminded again this 

15   morning that all glory is Thine, both now and 

16   forever, and even so come Lord Jesus.  Swing 

17   low, sweet chariot, coming for to carry us home.  

18   Thou art worthy.  Be glorified today in the 

19   convocation of the New York State Senate.  And I 

20   pray in Jesus' name, amen.  

21                Thank you.

11                THE SECRETARY:   Legislative 

12   Resolution Number 348, by Senator Murphy, 

13   honoring Officer Paul DeSousa of the 

14   Westchester County Police Department in 

15   recognition of his heroic action in saving a 

16   young pedestrian from serious injury.

17                ACTING PRESIDENT GRIFFO:   Senator 

18   Murphy.  

19                I'd ask for some order in the house, 

20   please.  If you can take your conversations 

21   outside the chamber.

22                Senator Murphy.

23                SENATOR MURPHY:   Thank you, 

24   Mr. President.  

25                I'd just like to recognize a true 


                                                                279

 1   hero in my community, Officer Paul DeSousa.  

 2                Paul was a graduate of Yorktown High 

 3   School in 2005.  He served our community as being 

 4   a volunteer firefighter and EMT.  He also served 

 5   our country in the armed forces, in Afghanistan 

 6   and Iraq.  And he continues to serve the people 

 7   of Westchester County as a Westchester County 

 8   police officer.

 9                On January 6th, during our first 

10   snowstorm down in Westchester, while 

11   Officer DeSousa was on patrol on the Saw Mill 

12   River Parkway, there was a 15-year-old boy 

13   walking across, and he stopped the car to make 

14   sure that the young boy was brought to safety.  

15   While doing so, a car slipped out of control, and 

16   Officer DeSousa hoisted the boy to the hood of 

17   his car while being hit.  

18                He is okay, I'd like to report.  And 

19   I'd just like to acknowledge his heroic efforts 

20   in saving a 15-year-old boy in the community.  

21                Thank you, Paul.

23   you, Senator Murphy.

15                THE SECRETARY:   Legislative 

16   Resolution Number 276, by Senators Skelos, Klein, 

17   Stewart-Cousins and Krueger, celebrating the life 

18   and career of former New York State Governor 

19   Mario M. Cuomo, and expressing sincerest sorrow 

20   upon the occasion of his death.  

21                "WHEREAS, It is the sense of this 

22   Legislative Body to recognize and commend those 

23   individuals of distinguished purpose whose lives 

24   have been committed to public service in the 

25   pursuit of excellence in the conduct of the 


                                                                281

 1   legislative process in this great Empire State; 

 2   and 

 3                "WHEREAS, Mario M. Cuomo, three-term 

 4   governor, died on Thursday, January 1, 2015, in 

 5   Manhattan, at the age of 82; and 

 6                "WHEREAS, Born in Queens on June 15, 

 7   1932, Mario Matthew Cuomo was the fourth child of 

 8   Andrea and Immaculata Cuomo; unable to speak 

 9   English, they came to the United States from the 

10   province of Salerno, south of Naples, settling at 

11   first in Jersey City, New Jersey; and 

12                "WHEREAS, Mario M. Cuomo grew up in 

13   the Queens neighborhood of South Jamaica; as a 

14   young boy, he worked alongside his family members 

15   at the grocery store which they owned and 

16   operated; and 

17                "WHEREAS, In 1949, after graduating 

18   from St. John's Preparatory School in Queens, 

19   Mario M. Cuomo pursued his love of baseball and 

20   played on the freshman baseball team at 

21   St. John's University; three years later, at the 

22   age of 19, he signed a contract to play center 

23   field for the Class D Brunswick Pirates in 

24   Georgia; and 

25                "WHEREAS, Due to an injury doing 


                                                                282

 1   what he loved best, his baseball career was 

 2   short-lived, and Mario M. Cuomo returned to his  

 3   studies and graduated in 1953 from St. John's 

 4   University, where he majored in Latin American 

 5   studies, English and philosophy; and 

 6                "WHEREAS, The recipient of a 

 7   scholarship, Mario M. Cuomo enrolled in 

 8   St. John's Law School; it was at this time he met 

 9   his future wife, Matilda N. Raffa, a fellow 

10   student; Mario and Matilda proudly raised five 

11   children; and 

12                "WHEREAS, Mario M. Cuomo's first 

13   position as a lawyer was serving as the 

14   confidential assistant to Judge Adrian P. Burke 

15   of the New York State Court of Appeals, which he 

16   would reshape 30 years later by appointing all 

17   seven members, including Judith S. Kaye, the 

18   first woman to serve as chief judge; and 

19                "WHEREAS, Mario M. Cuomo joined a 

20   Brooklyn law firm, Corner, Weisbrod, Froeb & 

21   Charles, in 1963, and the following year began 

22   his distinguished service to the public; and 

23                "WHEREAS, 1974 was the year Mario M. 

24   Cuomo entered politics and was named Secretary of 

25   State; in this capacity, he was responsible for 


                                                                283

 1   numerous tasks, some of which included settling 

 2   strikes as well as mediating land disputes; and   

 3                "WHEREAS, Four years later, Hugh L. 

 4   Carey was reelected Governor of the State of 

 5   New York, and Mario M. Cuomo was elected as 

 6   Lieutenant Governor; and 

 7                "WHEREAS, On November 2, 1982, at 

 8   age 50, Mario M. Cuomo became the 52nd man to be 

 9   elected New York's governor, defeating 

10   businessman Lewis E. Lehrman by approximately 

11   180,000 votes; and 

12                "WHEREAS, A resolute leader and 

13   renowned orator, Mario M. Cuomo delivered the 

14   keynote address at the 1984 Democratic National 

15   Convention in San Francisco, the speech which was 

16   the high-water mark of his national political 

17   career; and 

18                "WHEREAS, Deciding not to run for 

19   President of the United States, Mario M. Cuomo 

20   focused his political energies to the citizens of 

21   the State of New York and, together with the 

22   Legislature, established a new ethics code which 

23   governed state and local officials and state 

24   employees; he proclaimed 1988 the beginning of 

25   the Decade of the Child, 1989 the Year to Fight 


                                                                284

 1   Drug Abuse, and when he won his third term as 

 2   Governor in 1990, the Year of the Environment; 

 3   and 

 4                "WHEREAS, Following his 

 5   extraordinary career in public office, Mario M. 

 6   Cuomo returned to Manhattan to work for the law 

 7   firm of Willkie Farr & Gallagher, write books and 

 8   give speeches; and 

 9                WHEREAS, In addition to his wife, 

10   Matilda N. Cuomo, Mario M. Cuomo is survived by 

11   his five children, Governor Andrew M. Cuomo, 

12   Dr. Margaret I. Cuomo, Maria Cuomo Cole, Madeline 

13   Cuomo O'Donohue, and Christopher Cuomo, as well 

14   as 14 grandchildren; and 

15                "WHEREAS, Every citizen in New York 

16   State has most certainly benefited, in one way or 

17   another, from the deep dedication and caring 

18   concern Mario M. Cuomo brought to his work as 

19   their Governor, a leader and selfless public 

20   servant; now, therefore, be it 

21                "RESOLVED, That this Legislative 

22   Body pause in its deliberations in a moment of 

23   silent tribute to Mario M. Cuomo, whose generous 

24   and thoughtful concern for the welfare of others 

25   enhanced the lives of those so fortunate to have 


                                                                285

 1   called him family, colleague and friend, and to 

 2   express its deepest condolences to his family; 

 3   and be it further 

 4                "RESOLVED, That a copy of this 

 5   resolution, suitably engrossed, be transmitted to 

 6   the family of Mario M. Cuomo."

 7                ACTING PRESIDENT GRIFFO:   Senator 

 8   Skelos.

 9                SENATOR SKELOS:   Thank you, 

10   Mr. President.  

11                Today we really celebrate the life 

12   of Mario Cuomo, a life well-lived -- well-lived 

13   in his own personal life and well-lived as 

14   Governor and an elected official.  

15                I think the most important part of 

16   Governor Cuomo's life was his family, his love of 

17   his wife Matilda, 60 years of marriage, and 

18   certainly all of his children and grandchildren.  

19   That was his priority.  

20                His religion, a person of deep faith 

21   who sometimes was challenged on that deep faith 

22   but always felt that he was doing the right 

23   thing.  And whether we agree with an elected 

24   official or anybody as to what they believe in, 

25   as long as it is from their heart and from their 


                                                                286

 1   brain, we have to respect that.  And that's where 

 2   Mario Cuomo's always was.  

 3                And certainly as Governor.  I had 

 4   the opportunity to serve with him when I was 

 5   first elected to the Senate in '84 and then 

 6   starting to serve in 1985.  What I learned very 

 7   quickly as a young Senator, when you had the 

 8   opportunity to meet with him on legislation -- at 

 9   that time I was chair of the Aging Committee -- 

10   you had to know your facts.  You had to be 

11   well-prepared.  Because even if he agreed with 

12   you, he had to challenge you a little bit, an 

13   intellectual challenge.  

14                And certainly it was a tough task.  

15   Because Mario Cuomo could take -- and I say this 

16   most respectfully -- both sides of the issue.  

17   But when he took both sides of the issue, it was 

18   trying to find a consensus as to what was the 

19   right thing to do.  And that's really what our 

20   jobs are, finding consensus, finding that middle 

21   ground so that we can govern well and we can do 

22   what's right for the people of the State of 

23   New York.

24                So I had the deepest respect for 

25   Governor Cuomo.  He was a good person.  As I 


                                                                287

 1   said, number one, a good family person, a man of 

 2   God.  And certainly when he governed in the 

 3   various capacities that he had, and certainly as 

 4   Governor of the State of New York, it came with 

 5   his heart and it came with his brain.  

 6                So to the entire Cuomo family, we 

 7   all had a deepest respect for Governor Cuomo.  

 8   And certainly today, rather than saying we mourn 

 9   his loss, which we do, but we really celebrate 

10   his life.  

11                Thank you, Mr. President.

12                ACTING PRESIDENT GRIFFO:   Thank 

13   you, Senator Skelos.  

14                Senator Stewart-Cousins.

15                SENATOR STEWART-COUSINS:   Yes, 

16   thank you.  

17                And thank you to my colleagues and  

18   Senator Skelos, Senator Klein and Senator Krueger 

19   in terms of making sure that we spend this moment 

20   celebrating the life of Mario Cuomo, Governor 

21   Mario Cuomo.  

22                And certainly I offer condolences to 

23   his family, as we have done since his death at 

24   the beginning of January.

25                I did not have the privilege of 


                                                                288

 1   serving with Governor Mario Cuomo, but I had the 

 2   privilege of knowing him outside of the formal 

 3   atmosphere of the Governor, where he would 

 4   explain to me the origin of my name -- because in 

 5   Italian, Andreas means "manly," and mine is the 

 6   feminine.  

 7                And we would talk about, you know, 

 8   the origins and the respect that he had not only 

 9   for how he grew up and how he lived, but what he 

10   saw as the vision for our state and our country, 

11   which we all know how well he articulated.

12                He was a great orator.  He was a 

13   great Governor.  He was a great public servant.  

14   And one of the things that I learned about him is 

15   what we received in the little booklet after his 

16   funeral, where there were these different 

17   excerpts of speeches.  And one of the things that 

18   he said he wanted on his tombstone is this simple 

19   two-word legacy:  "He tried."  

20                He tried.  But not only did he try, 

21   he did.  He created opportunities for people who 

22   would not have opportunities, because he 

23   understood how it was being that person outside 

24   of what society would normally have inside.  And 

25   he spent a life dedicated to breaking barriers, 


                                                                289

 1   and he did that on our Court of Appeals.  He did 

 2   name the first two female judges.  He named the 

 3   first African-American judge, the first Hispanic 

 4   judges.  He was that person who not only said 

 5   what he meant, but did what he said.  

 6                And obviously we all know the legacy 

 7   of his vetoing the death penalty seven times.  A 

 8   man of principle.  He talked the talk, he walked 

 9   the walk.  He removed barriers.  He elevated 

10   people who would not normally be elevated.  He 

11   was indeed an exemplary public servant, and 

12   someone that we do owe a debt of gratitude to.

13                So again, it is a celebration of his 

14   life, of his legacy and his history that we 

15   should embrace and follow.

16                Thank you.

17                ACTING PRESIDENT GRIFFO:   Thank 

18   you, Senator Stewart-Cousins.  

19                Senator Valesky.

20                SENATOR VALESKY:   Thank you, 

21   Mr. President.  

22                And on behalf of Senator Klein and 

23   certainly all of the members of the Independent 

24   Democratic Conference, I want to acknowledge the 

25   tremendous loss that our Governor and his family 


                                                                290

 1   have endured these past few weeks.  We again 

 2   extend our deepest condolences, our sympathies 

 3   and our prayers to Matilda Cuomo, to Governor 

 4   Andrew Cuomo and the entire Cuomo family as they 

 5   endure this challenging time.

 6                Certainly the pain of losing a loved 

 7   one never goes away, especially a parent.  In 

 8   many cases they are our anchors, the strong, 

 9   dependable force that keeps us safe during the 

10   storms and steady during rough waters.  

11                As we pay our respects to former 

12   Governor Mario Cuomo today, we acknowledge that 

13   not only was he a man of deep faith and 

14   commitment to family, but an honorable man 

15   devoted and dedicated to the people of the great 

16   State of New York.  He dedicated his life to a 

17   career in public service, and that career was one 

18   of unparalleled success and of the highest 

19   regard.

20                As a New York Democrat interested in 

21   public civil service some 25 years ago, Governor 

22   Mario Cuomo was for me and many of us a 

23   Democratic touchstone.  His eloquence, 

24   authenticity, candor and intellect were a 

25   constant inspiration and stellar example to those 


                                                                291

 1   of us learning how we too could make a difference 

 2   in the lives of New Yorkers.  

 3                Witnessing firsthand not just his 

 4   political finesse but his common sense and 

 5   powerful insight into what the citizens of 

 6   New York State needed and deserved was truly 

 7   something remarkable to watch.  And the lessons I 

 8   learned and many of us here learned from him have 

 9   stayed with me and have stayed with us during our 

10   careers here in public service.  

11                His grand presence will be sorely 

12   missed.  And perhaps one of the greatest tributes 

13   we can offer is to remain committed to his spirit 

14   of commonsense governing, of getting the job done 

15   and doing what is right for the many, not the 

16   few.  

17                While former Governor Mario Cuomo 

18   may no longer be with us, his spirit, his 

19   presence and his legacy will surround us always.  

20                Thank you.

21                ACTING PRESIDENT GRIFFO:   Thank 

22   you, Senator Valesky.

23                Senator Gianaris.

24                SENATOR GIANARIS:   Thank you, 

25   Mr. President.  


                                                                292

 1                Much has been said about the life of 

 2   Mario Cuomo in the last month and indeed here in 

 3   this chamber.  And I don't want to be redundant, 

 4   but I do want to add my personal remembrances, 

 5   because he was a leader not just in New York but 

 6   in this country for a very particular 

 7   demographic.  

 8                And as the son of immigrants, 

 9   parents from Queens myself, as Mario Cuomo was, 

10   he was someone who showed the way, of how to come 

11   to this country in the first or second generation 

12   and take one's place in government, take one's 

13   place as a leader in one's community.  

14                And I was privileged to have my 

15   first job in government be for then-Governor 

16   Cuomo over 20 years ago, representing him in the 

17   County of Queens, and learned so much about the 

18   values one should bring to government.  

19                It's easy to -- as I think our 

20   opening prayer said today, it's easy to be 

21   tempted, it's easy to lose sight of what's 

22   important on a day-to-day basis in these 

23   positions that we hold.  But he was one who never 

24   lost sight of the important things, the important 

25   values of caring for others, of giving voice to 


                                                                293

 1   the voiceless.  

 2                We have a phrase that you hear a lot 

 3   today, speaking truth to power.  Well, Mario 

 4   Cuomo was the ultimate example of speaking truth 

 5   to power before anyone had uttered that phrase 

 6   for the first time.  

 7                And so for me, he had a profound 

 8   impact on my life.  He is responsible for my 

 9   getting into public service, even to the point 

10   where he was kind enough to host one of my first 

11   fundraisers when I ran for the Assembly some 

12   15 years ago.  

13                I will certainly never forget the 

14   impact he had on my life, and I think the same 

15   can be said for all New Yorkers.  

16                Thank you.

17                ACTING PRESIDENT GRIFFO:   Thank 

18   you, Senator Gianaris.

19                Senator Farley.

20                SENATOR FARLEY:   Thank you, 

21   Mr. President.

22                I rise to pay tribute to not only a 

23   great person but a great Governor.  Mario Cuomo 

24   and I, our careers actually paralleled each 

25   other.  And I've known him since he's been a 


                                                                294

 1   Secretary of State, Lieutenant Governor and 

 2   Governor, and considered him a very close 

 3   personal friend.  

 4                Incidentally, when he was 

 5   Lieutenant Governor he used to spend a lot of 

 6   time in this chamber presiding and was very much 

 7   a part of the Senate.

 8                Mario Cuomo has been -- so much has 

 9   been mentioned about him.  But I'll tell you, he 

10   used to call me at all times -- I think I was on 

11   speed dial -- early in the morning and this and 

12   that.  He was always very kind to my family, 

13   calling my aunt when she had her 100th birthday, 

14   and doing various personal things.  

15                And Mario Cuomo was a person that 

16   his family came first.  I think one of the 

17   greatest love affairs that I've ever seen is 

18   between he and Matilda.  He was absolutely 

19   devoted to her.  And what a remarkable woman she 

20   is.  

21                As I saw her at the Mansion and she 

22   told me about his last few days, he was such a 

23   strong person.  But particularly later in life 

24   with his heart problem, which was almost 

25   incurable, he suffered a lot.


                                                                295

 1                Mario Cuomo was devoted to the State 

 2   of New York and to his family, but he was always 

 3   an underdog rooter.  He was always for the 

 4   underdog.  And, you know, as competitive as 

 5   anybody that I ever knew.  Anybody that competed 

 6   against him in basketball, it was mentioned at 

 7   his funeral, or any other place, he was very 

 8   aggressive.  

 9                But he also had a very kind and 

10   gentle nature about him.  He was a remarkable 

11   man, a remarkable Governor.  And my very best to 

12   his family at this great loss, because it was a 

13   terrible loss to his remarkable family and he 

14   does have a beautiful family.  

15                And Mario Cuomo, the State of 

16   New York has been better off because of your 

17   service.

18                Thank you, Mr. President.

19                ACTING PRESIDENT GRIFFO:   Thank 

20   you, Senator Farley.

21                Senator Hassell-Thompson.

22                SENATOR SKELOS:   Thank you, 

23   Mr. President.  

24                I rise too to pay my tribute to 

25   Governor Mario Cuomo, who I knew to be a 


                                                                296

 1   tremendous gentleman who epitomized the American 

 2   dream.  And as we all know, he was the son of an 

 3   immigrant, but he saw firsthand the value of hard 

 4   work.  And these are early lessons that he
